# NVIDIA OpenShell Helm Chart

Verified: 2026-08-25 against chart v0.0.111
Provenance: read from the chart templates while deploying the gateway on k3s
under Argo CD

Upstream marks this chart experimental and states templates, values, and
defaults change between releases. Re-verify on any bump.

## Naming

The chart's `name` is **`helm-chart`** — the chart name becomes the OCI image
path (`ghcr.io/nvidia/openshell/helm-chart`), so it cannot be the product name.
That feeds the stock Helm fullname helper:

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| `.Chart.Name` | `helm-chart` |
| chart default `nameOverride` | `openshell` |
| `openshell.name` | `openshell` |
| `openshell.fullname` | release name if it contains `openshell`, else `<release>-openshell` |

A release named `openshell` therefore yields resources named `openshell` — from
an upstream default, not from anything in your values. Set `fullnameOverride`
explicitly if downstream config depends on the resulting names.

### fullname controls names; it does not control labels

| Governed by `fullnameOverride` | Governed by `nameOverride` + release name |
|---|---|
| StatefulSet / Deployment, its pod, its PVC | `app.kubernetes.io/name` |
| Service | `app.kubernetes.io/instance` |
| ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding, ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding | |
| certgen PKI secrets | |

`openshell.selectorLabels` is built from `openshell.name` and `.Release.Name`,
so external Services and ServiceMonitors selecting on `app.kubernetes.io/name`
survive a `fullnameOverride` change untouched.

**The same fact is a rename hazard.** `StatefulSet.spec.selector.matchLabels`
also uses `openshell.selectorLabels`, so a renamed StatefulSet carries a
selector identical to the old one. Two StatefulSets matching the same labels is
undefined behaviour in Kubernetes, and under GitOps with `prune: false` the old
one is not removed automatically. Delete it before the new one is created.

A renamed StatefulSet also provisions a **new, empty PVC**. The gateway's SQLite
database — providers, gateway registrations, sandbox records — stays on the old
volume.

## Credential key-encryption key breaks under `helm template`

`templates/credential-storage-key-encryption-key-secret.yaml`:

```gotemplate
{{- $existing := lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace $secretName -}}
{{- $encodedKeyEncryptionKey := randBytes 32 | b64enc -}}
{{- if $existing -}} ...reuse... {{- end }}
```

`lookup` returns nil under `helm template`, which is how Argo CD renders. Every
render mints a **new** KEK: the Application never converges, and with
`selfHeal: true` the rotating key makes stored provider credentials
undecryptable. `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` does not help — that is
Helm-uninstall semantics, not Argo-apply.

Both escapes skip the generation branch entirely:

- `server.credentialStorage.existingSecret` — a Secret you manage, with key
  `key-encryption-key` holding base64 of 32 random bytes.
- `server.credentialDrivers.kubernetesSecrets.enabled` — stores credentials as
  Kubernetes Secrets instead. Its RBAC Role grants read/write on **all** Secrets
  in the configured namespace.

## Agent Sandbox preflight hard-fails rendering

From v0.0.112, `templates/agent-sandbox-preflight.yaml` calls `fail` unless
`.Capabilities.APIVersions` reports `agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` or `v1alpha1`.
Under a renderer that does not supply cluster API versions the whole Application
fails to render, with the `fail` string verbatim in its status.
`agentSandbox.preflight.enabled=false` is the documented escape for offline
rendering. Charts at v0.0.111 and below have no preflight.

Agent Sandbox v0.4.6 serves `v1alpha1` only.

## Values behaviour worth knowing

| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `server.grpcEndpoint` | Empty derives correctly from `disableTls`: `ternary "http" "https"`, then `<fullname>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local:<port>`. No override needed for a plaintext gateway. |
| `supervisor.sideloadMethod` | Empty auto-detects on `.Capabilities.KubeVersion` — `image-volume` at k8s ≥1.35, else `init-container`. A cluster upgrade silently changes it. |
| `server.appArmorProfile` | Defaults to `Unconfined`, because runtime-default AppArmor can block the supervisor's network-namespace mount setup. That value is forbidden under PodSecurity `restricted` and `baseline`. |
| `server.workspaceStorageClass` | Empty omits `storageClassName` on sandbox workspace PVCs, so they land on the cluster default. Set it explicitly when the default is not the class you want them backed by. |
| `service.annotations` | Not rendered — `templates/service.yaml` has no `metadata.annotations` block. Exposing the gateway through an annotation-driven controller needs a sibling Service. |

## CLI and packaging

- **No client/server version negotiation.** Skew surfaces per-RPC as
  `Code::Unimplemented`, with messages like "whoami is not supported by this
  gateway version" — which reads as a missing feature rather than a version
  problem. Pin the CLI to the gateway's appVersion.
- **PyPI `openshell` ships `manylinux_2_39` wheels and no sdist.** A base image
  with glibc < 2.39 (Debian bookworm is 2.36) cannot install it at any version.
  Trixie (2.41) and Ubuntu noble (2.39) work.
- Upstream publishes **gateway** and **supervisor** container images but no CLI
  runtime image, so a CLI pod means `pip install` into a Python image.
